So I don't know if Voaters are super up to date with what's happening at South African universities but there's been a shittonne of protests about 'decolonising' the universities ie removing 'whiteness.'

It started with Rhodes Must Fall, which was a campaign to remove the statue of Cecil John Rhodes from the University of Cape Town. I didn't really agree but I could at least understand. I don't think it's right that the man who practically founded the university got his statue removed but I can appreciate why people didn't approve of his having a statue. Then protesters burned all the art inside the main residences, because the art was by white people and burning it was purging the university of whiteness. Then they started petrol bombing buses.

At my alma mater, Stellenbosch University, a group of students has been basically terrorising campus since the start of the year. Firstly, there was the 'Purpleface Incident.' Some girls painted themselves purple and posted a picture on Instagram. Open Stellenbosch, this organisation I mentioned, began a harassment campaign against them, saying that they intentionally used a dark filter on their Instagram in order to replicate blackface. They posted the girls' information on social media and encouraged a witch hunt against them. They reported them to the university for racism and got them suspended. For painting themselves purple for a party.

http://www.news24.com/SouthAfrica/News/open-stellenbosch-retracts-apology-to-suspended-blackface-students-20160209 Now they are demanding the removal of the statue of JS Marais. There is nothing to suggest that Marais was racist, like there is for Rhodes. He was a good man who donated all he owned to the university to help get it started. But he's white, so his statue must go. As part of the protests they vandalised the law building Wednesday night, raided a semester test at the economics building last night, set fire to Admin B and have now chained shut the doors of the student centre, trapping everyone inside.

I wouldn't care, because hey, in my mind the university raised this monster. They catered to all their demands, they have modules where we learned about how society is a white man's patriarchy, even though this is South Africa of all places, and now they can lie in the bed they made. But my little brother is here now, and his education and safety are being held hostage by a group of students who seem to want to burn the university down. He was so excited to be a university student and play sports with some of the best, and now he can't because of one student organisation. And bear in mind that student participation in Open Stellenbosch is so poor that whenever they have a protest they need to bus in students from other universities and unemployed EFF supporters to get their numbers up.

And the university has done nothing. They know who the leaders of the movement are. They have a facebook page where they take selfies and brag about their criminal misconduct. It is all well documented. Yet the university does nothing. It has pressed absolutely no charges against anyone. Despite the fact that they have an obligation to create a safe environment for its students and it has evidence of exactly who is responsible for what, it does nothing but cater to the demands of an incredibly unpopular mob. Which makes no sense to me, because 'removing whiteness' is despicably vague. When will they be satisfied that the university has been purged of whiteness? When there are no more non-black students? When the university buildings are burnt to the ground? I don't understand why the university is risking my brother's safety for such bullshit. And I don't know if there's anything I can do about it. I don't feel safe driving my brother to campus anymore, but if he misses classes he fails. But students who miss classes to protest, they don't, because they have a right to protest, but my brother apparently doesn't have the right to feel safe.

What the fuck.

EDIT: I would just like to say that I'm very grateful for the kind words and advice. People often say sympathy is empty but it means a lot to have people from around the world offer theirs. Often in South Africa it feels like nobody cares about your problems because they don't fit into the narratives people like to weave about Africa, so to hear kind words from people I neither know nor have any kind of investment in my happiness is quite lovely and I'm very thankful.

**Daily Devotional**

**March 11**

*20 But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, (Jude 1:20 KJV)*

This verse is talking about praying in tongues, which is one of the gifts of the Holy Spirit. All Christians who have been born again, and baptized as Jesus commanded (Matthew 28:19), have this gift of speaking in tongues (1 Corinthians 14). Non-Christians cannot operate in the Gifts of the Holy Spirit, as you must be a born again Christian, to be able to receive the Holy Spirit (John 14:16-17), and to have the Gifts.

Why religion today, mostly teach against the Spiritual Gifts and speaking in tongues, I don’t understand, as that is what the early believers and the Disciples all needed to have the power that they displayed in their ministries. The bible says to forbid not the speaking in tongues (1 Corinthians 14:39). Why the Christians now don’t want the power of the Holy Spirit in their lives is hard to understand. The speaking in tongues is a powerful way to increase our most holy faith, and it edifies and gives rest to the believer. All the Gifts of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:8-10) should be used by the Christian to demonstrate the power of God, and thereby glorify Him. Thank you Lord for the Gifts.
